newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Park May to lay off workers to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Park May to lay off workers to cut costs.

text.p: Transport services firm Park May Bhd plans reduce costs by trimming its manpower by 560 workers, the national Bernama news agency quoted company chairman Mohammed Hanif Omar as saying on Wednesday.
The company plans to lay off the employees in a two-phase exercise, he told reporters after the company's annual meeting here.
The first phase would involve the retrenchment of about 140 station masters under Park May's plan to rationalise its depot and bus station operations.
The second phase involves 300 bus conductors to be made redundant as the company is introducing one-man operated buses which replace the conductor with a ticketing machine, Hanif said.
Bernama did not say when the planned lay-offs will start and from which departments the remaining 120 workers to be retrenched would come.
The report also did not state the total number of workers at the company, which is 50 percent owned by conglomerate Renong Bhd.
Park May officials could not be reached for comment.
Hanif said the workers to be retrenched under the first phase will receive an eight-month pay package and those in the second phase six-and-a-half-month pay settlement as retrenchment benefits.
"The staff identified for this have agreed subject to the benefits that the company is offering," he said.
Park May plans to expand its fleet of buses by between 80 and 100 buses annually, he said.
